description: The Banking Deserts Dashboard identifies banking deserts, census tracts with no bank branch inside them or within a radius of their population centre of 2 miles in urban, 5 miles in suburban and 10 miles in rural areas, and potential banking deserts, tracts that would become deserts if one branch closed, tracking the decline of bank branches in the United States. It is published on FedCommunities, the Federal Reserve's community development site, using S&P SNL branch data and US Census TIGER/Line boundaries, with a stricter definition of an active branch than interagency data and retroactive updates for closures in 2020 and 2021. Coverage is the United States, with state and county figures from 2019 to 2025; the page was last updated on 3 November 2025. The dashboard, a 40 MB zip of data and a PDF report are available free online, updated annually, and are intended for informational and educational purposes. Caveats: branch data come from a commercial source, values are missing for tracts with insufficient income data, and online banking is not counted. For simulation it maps where communities depend on few branches, showing where a branch closure or disaster would cut physical access to banking services. It is related to the FDIC BankFind Suite record in this catalogue, which lists bank branches.
